details.body: VACANCY: I The state:(1) SUnyatA;(2) riktatA.II Vacant post, etc.:(1) SUnyam; (2) riktam.
VACANCY , s. SUnyatA -tvaM, riktatA -tvaM, SUnyaM, riktaM. — (Of a throne, &c.) arAjakatvaM, anAyakatvaM, asvAmikatvaM.

Vacant, a. SUnya, (fig. also), rikta; ‘with v; looks’ SUnyekzaRa a.; ‘v(acant) minded’ SUnyahfdaya. 2 asvAmika; ‘a v(acant) throne’ arAjaka. Vacancy, s. SUnyaM, riktaM. 2 SUnyaM; asvAmikaM aDikArapadaM. Vacate, v. t. utsfj 6 P, ric 7 P, pari-, tyaj 1 P. [Vacat]ion, s. anaDyayanaM, aDya-yanaviSrAmaH-nivftti f., viSrAmakAlaH.

VACANT: SUnya (f. nyA), placing me in v. (throne): SUnye saMpraRiDAya mAm, Mah. iv. 38. 17.; scarcely went towards her house with a v. mind: SUnyA jagAma BavanABimuKI kaTaYcit, Ku. iii. 75.; having v. looks: SUnyAkfti (mfn.), Ki. xvii. 39.: v. Also empty, free, unoccupied.

VACANT , a. (Empty) SUnyaH -nyA -nyaM, riktaH -ktA -ktaM, vitAnaH -nA -naM, KilaH -lA -laM. — (Unoccupied) asvAmikaH -kA -kaM, anAyakaH &c. ‘as a throne,’ arAjakaH -kA -kaM. — (Empty of thought,) vicA- ralakzaRaSUnyaH -nyA -nyaM; ‘vacant gaze,’ SUnyekzaRaM.
VACATE: utsfjati (sfj, c. 6.): v. To relin- -quish, leave, empty.
To VACATE , v. a. utsfj (c. 6. -sfjati -srazwuM), tyaj, SUnyIkf.
VACATION: (1) avakASaH (?);(2) virAmaH (?).
VACATION , s. avakASaH, aDyayanavirAmaH, aDyayananivfttiH f., anaDyAyaH.
Vaccinate, v. t. gobIjaM niviS c.
VACCINATE: gobIjaM niveSayati (c. of viS) (?).
To VACCINATE , v. a. raktavarawInivAraRArTaM or vasantaroganivAraRArTaM gosPo- wapUyalavaM bAhumAMse niviS (c. 10. -veSayati -yituM).
VACCINATION: gobIjaniveSanam (?) and sim. comp. s.
VACCINATION , s. bAhumAMse gosPowapUyalavaniveSanaM.
Vaccine, a. gavya.
VACCINE: I Cow's: gavya (f. vyA).II Of vaccination: by comp.
VACCINE , a. gavyaH -vyA -vyaM, gosambanDI &c., govizayakaH -kA -kaM.
Vacillate, See Waver. [Vacillat]ion, s. asTiratA, aniScayaH, cAMcalyaM.
VACILLATE: dolAyate (nomi.): v. To waver, swing.
To VACILLATE , v. n. dola (nom. dolAyate), vical. See To WAVER
VACILLATING (adj.): of men: asTira (f. rA): v. Fickle.
VACILLATION: asTiratA: v. Fickleness, in- -constancy.
VACILLATION , s. caYcalatvaM -tA, cAYcalyaM, vicalanaM, AndolanaM.
Vacuity, Vacuum, s. SUnyaM, KaM, riktaM, AkASaM.
VACUITY, VACUUM: (1) SUnyam;(2) Kam (rare).
VACUITY , s. SUnyatA, riktatA, SUnyaM, riktaM, SuziraM, KaM, see HOLE.
VACUUM , s. SUnyaM, riktaM, SUnyatA, riktatA -tvaM, nirvARaM.
Vagabond, a., s. svecCAcArin, pariBramin; yaTecCavihArin. 2 ajYAtanivAsa, gUQacArin.
VAGABOND: (1) avijYAtanivAsa (f. sA), Mit. and sim. comp. s; gUQacArin (f. RI), M. n. ix. 260.; he leads a v. life: sa gUQaM carati vAso na jYAtaH.
VAGABOND , a. or s. aDvagaH -gA -gaM, cakrAwaH -wA -waM, avanicaraH &c., BramI -miRI -mi (n), pariBramI &c., BramaRakArI &c., deSAwanakArI m.
Vagary, s. vi, BramaH, CaMdaH-das n., mano-lOlyaM, budDicApalyaM.
VAGARY: (1) BramiH (?);(2) BrAntam, vi- (?).
VAGARY , s. manolOlyaM, budDivilAsaH, budDicApalyaM, unmArgaH.
VAGRANCY: *gUQacArivizayako viDiH.
VAGRANCY , s. aDvaBramaRaM, aDvaparyawanaM, mArgapatiBfmaRaM.
VAGRANT , s. mArgapariBramI m. (n), aSudDavAsakaH. See VAGABOND.
Vague, a. aniScita, saMdigDa, aniyata, anirRIta, aparicCinna [Vague]ness, s. aniScayaH aparicCedaH, anirRayaH, saMdehaH, saMSayaH.
VAGUE: (1) aniScita (f. tA): v. Uncertain; (2) sandigDa (f. gDA): v. Doubtful.
VAGUE , a. aniyataH -tA -taM, avivakzitaH &c. See INDETERMINATE.
VAGUELY: (1) aniScitam: v. Uncertainly; (2) sandigDam = doubtfully.
VAGUENESS: (1) aniScayaH (=uncertainty);(2) sandigDatA (= doubtfulness).
VAGUENESS , s. aniyatatvaM, anirRayaH, avivakzA, avivakzitatvaM.

Vain, a. vyarTa, nizPala, viPala, nirarTaka, moGa, muDA-vfTA in comp.; ‘v(ain) thoughts’ vfTAmanoraTAH. 2 asAra, niHsAra, SUnya. 3 (Vainglorious) vfTABimAnin, ahaMkArin, vfTAvalepa, garvita; See Proud. [Vain]ly, ‘in v(ain)’, adv. vfTA, muDA, nirarTakaM, vyarTaM, nizPalaM. Vanity, s. vfTABimAnaH, miTyAgarvaH, ahaMkAraH; See Pride. 2 asAratvaM, niHsAratA, avalepaH, vEyarTyaM, moGatA. 3 asAradravyaM.

VAIN: I In gen.:(1) nizPala (f. lA = fruit- -less: q. v.), one whose efforts are v.: nizPala- prayatna (f. tnA), M. n. on Ki. ix. 46.;(2) nirarTaka (f. rTikA = useless: q. v.), advice is now v.: idAnIM nirarTakAH Kalu upadeSAH, K.;(3) vyarTa (f. rTA = 2.);(4) moGa (f. GA), made her hand v.: tatpARiM moGaM vitene, N. iii. 5.;(5) vfTA- in comp.: v. jest: vfTAparIhAsaH, N. ix. 25.; (your) toils are v.: vfTASramaH, Ki. v. 45.II Proud: vfTABimAnin (f. nI), and sim. comp. s. III Showy, ostentatious: q. v.

VAIN, IN-, VAINLY: vfTA, do not talk in v.: na vfTA vAkyaM samuccAryatAm, J.; (2) vyarTam, and why are you tiring yourself in v.: vyarTa pariSrAmyasi vA kimarTam, N. iii. 13.;(3) muDA, why in vain: kimarTa muDA, Ve. iii. 4.;(4) nirarTakam (= 2); (5) nizPalam (= fruitlessly).

VAIN , a. (Empty, worthless) SUnyaH -nyA -nyaM, riktaH -ktA -ktaM, asAraH -rA -raM, niHsAraH &c., nirarTakaH &c., see EMPTY. — (Fruitless, un- availing) nirarTakaH -kA -kaM, anarTakaH &c., vyarTaH -rTA -rTaM, moGaH -GA -GaM, nizPalaH -lA -laM, kadarTaH &c., klIvaH -vA -vaM, vfTA in comp.; ‘indulging vain hopes,’ moGASaH -SA -SaM. — (Conceited) aBi- mAnI -ninI -ni (n), AtmABimAnI &c., mAnI &c., ahaNkArI &c., [Page826-a+ 51] sABimAnaH -nA -naM, sAhaNkAraH -rA -raM, ahammAnI &c., garvitaH -tA -taM, see CONCEITED; ‘of one's appearance,’ darSanIyamAnI &c. — (In vain) vfTA, muDA, see VAINLY; ‘laboring in vain,’ vfTodyamaH -mA -maM, BagnodyamaH &c.
VAINGLORIOUS: vfTABimAnin (f. nI) and sim. comp. s: v. Boastful.
VAINLY , adv. vfTA, muDA, moGaM, vyarTatas, vyarTaM, nizPalaM.
VAISYA , s. (Man of the third tribe, or of the class of mer- chants and husbandmen, fabled as sprung from the thigh of Brahmā) vESyaH, viw m. (S), UrujaH, UravyaH, aryyaH, BUmi- spfk m. (S).
VALE: upatyakA: v. Valley.
VALE , s. darI -rA, IzannimnaBUmiH f. See VALLEY.
Valediction, s. AmaMtraRaM, ApfcCA, ApracCanaM; svastivAdaH. Valedictory, a. svastivAcanika (kI f.).
VALEDICTION: AmantraRam: v. Farewell.
VALEDICTION , s. AmantraRaM, ApracCanaM, ASIrvAdaH, prAsTAnikASIrvacanaM, prasTAnakAle svastivacanaM, prAsTAnikasvastivacanaM.
VALEDICTORY , a. AmantrayitA -trI -tf (tf), ASIrvAdI -dinI &c., svasti- vAcanikaH -kI -kaM, ASIrvAdAtmakaH -kA -kaM, svastivacanarUpaH &c.
VALERIAN: a plant: jananI (Wilson).
VALERIAN , s. (Plant) jananI, miziH -zI f., pravrajitA.
Valet, s. cewaH, dAsaH, pArSvacaraH.
VALET: (1) pArSvacaraH;(2) pArSvikaH;(3) cewaH.
VALET , s. pArSvikaH, vastraparikalpakaH, pArSvAnucaraH, sErinDraH.
Valetudinarian, a., s. rogin, durbala, vyADipIqita, sadArogin.
VALETUDINARIAN: (1) rogin (f. RI = sickly); (2) durbala (f. lA = weak).
VALETUDINARIAN , s. svAsTyArTI m. (n), ArogyArTI m., sadArogI m.
Valiant, a. vikrAMta, parAkramavat, uruvikrama, SUra, vIra; See Brave. [Valiant]ly, adv. savikramaM, saparAkramaM, SUra-vIra-vat, sAhasapUrvakaM.
VALIANT: (1) vikrAntaH (f. ntA);(2) parAkrAnta (f. ntA);(3) parAkramaSAlin (f. nI); etc.: v. Also brave, strong.
VALIANT , a. vikrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, vIraH -rA -raM, uruvikramaH -mA -maM, BawaH -wA -waM, UrjitaH &c., see HEROIC; ‘is valiant,’ vikramate -ti, parAkramati.
VALIANTLY: (1) sAhasapUrvakam;(2) savikramam, etc.
Valid, a. sabala, prabala, sapramARa; sayuktika. (kI f.), aKaMqya, nyAyya, Darmya. [Valid]ity, s. prAbalyaM, sidDi f.
VALID: (1) prabala (f. lA);(2) balavat (f. tI): v. Strong, sound, good.

VALID , a. (Sound, just, that can be supported) sapramARaH -RA -RaM, supramARakaH -kA -kaM, sidDapramARaH &c., suprAmARikaH -kI -kaM, vajrapramARakaH -kA -kaM, prabalaH -lA -laM, sabalaH &c., aKaRqanIyaH -yA -yaM, sidDaH -dDA -dDaM, DarmyaH -rmyA -rmyaM, aviSudDaH -dDA -dDaM, nizpannaH -nnA -nnaM, valavAn -vatI &c., sapraBAvaH -vA -vaM, dfQaH -QA -QaM. — (Having legal force) vyavahAropayogI -ginI &c., vyavahArasamarTaH -rTA -rTaM, vyavahArasADakaH -DikA -kaM.
VALIDITY: (1) prabalatA;(2) prAbalyam;(3) balavattvam, -ttAH v. Strength, soundness.
VALIDITY , s. sapramARatA -tvaM, sabalatA, prabalatA, prAbalyaM, praBAvaH, sapra- BAvatvaM, aKaRqanIyatA, sidDiH f., sidDatA, nizpattiH f., DarmyatA. — (In law) vyavahAropayogitA, vyavahArasAmarTyaM.
Valise, s. carma-maMjuzA-pewakaH.
Valley, Vale, s. darI, upatyakA, adridroRI.
VALLEY: (1) upatyakA;(2) droRI (Wilson).
VALLEY , s. darI -rA, kandaraH -rI, darIBUH f., darIBUmiH f., upatyakA, droRI, parvatadroRI, adridroRI, nimnaBUH f., nimnaBUmiH f., prAntaraM, SOlo- paSalyaM, parvatadvayamaDyaBUmiH f.
Vallum, s. prAkAraH, vapraH.
Valor, s. vi-parA-kramaH, SOryaM, vIryaM. [Valor]ous, a. SUra, vIra, vikrAMta; See Brave.
VALOROUS: vikrAnta (f. ntA): v. Valiant, brave.
VALOROUS , a. vikrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, SUraH -rA -raM. See VALIANT.
VALOUR: (1) vikramaH;(2) parAkramaH;(3) vikrAntiH: v. Also boldness, prowess, strength.
VALOUR , s. vIryyaM, SOryyaM, vikramaH, parAkramaH. See HEROISM.
VALUABLE: I Adj.: bahumUlya (f. lyA) and sim. comp. s: v. Costly, rich.II Subs.: (1) bahumUlyadravyam and sim. expr. s.

VALUAELE , a. mahAmUlyaH -lyA -lyaM, bahumUlyaH &c., mahArGaH -rGA -rGaM, arGyaH -rGyA -rGyaM, arGArhaH -rhA -rhaM, mahArhaH &c., bahumAnayitavyaH -vyA -vyaM, maho- pakArakaH &c., guRavAn -vatI -vat (t). See PRECIOUS.
VALUATION: mUlyanirupaRam and sim. comp. s.
VALUATION , s. mUlyanirUpaRaM, mUlyasTApanaM -nA, arGasTApanaM -nA, mUlyapramA- RasTApanaM, arGaparimARanirUpaRaM, mUlyanirRayaH.

Value, v. t. mUlyaM-arDaM-nirUp 10 or sTA c. (sTApayati) or saMKyA c. 2 man 4 A, vi-gaR 10, Akal 10; ‘v(alue) highly’, bahu man-saMman c. s. mUlyaM, arGaH; See Price. 2 mAhAtmya, gariman m., sasAratA. 3 mahArGaH, bahu-mahA-mUlyaM. 4 arGapramARaM; ‘fixing the v(alue)’ arGasaMKyApanaM. [Valu]able, a. mahArha-rGa, mahA-bahu-mUlya, mUlyavat, guRavat. s. bahumUlyadravyaM. [Valu]ation, s. mUlyanirUpaRaM-saMKyA-panaM-nirRayaH.
VALUE (subs.): I Price (lit. and fig.): q. v.:(1) mUlyam;(2) arGaH, as it is above all value: anarGatvAt, H.II Precise import: SaktiH.

VALUE (v.): I Lit.: mUlyaM or arGaM nirUpayati (rUp, c. 10.) or sTApayati, saM- (c. of sTA).II Estimate: q. v.:(1) manyate (man, c. 4.), to v. much: bahu manyate, An.;(2) Akalayati (kal, c. 10.): v. To consider.

VALUE , s. (Price) mUlyaM, arGaH, see PRICE. — (Degree of price) mUlyapramARaM, arGapramARaM, mUlyaparimARaM, arGamitiH f., mitiH f., see RATE. — (High rate or estimation) mahAmUlyaM, bahumUlyaM, mahArGaH, bahu- mAnaM, bahumatiH f. — (Real worth) sAratA.
To VALUE , v. a. mUlyaM nirUp or sTA in caus., see To RATE — (Esteem) man (c. 10. mAnayati -yituM), see To ESTEEM; ‘highly,’ bahu man.
VALUED , p. p. or a. bahumataH -tA -taM, bahumAnitaH &c., sammAnitaH &c.
VALUER: I Lit.:(1) mUlyanirUpaka (f. pikA); (2) arGasaMsTApaka (f. pikA).II Fig.: expr. ed by verb.
Valve, s. kapA(vA)waH-wI-waM; piDAnaM.
VALVE: I Of a door: kapA(vA)wa (mfn.).II Of a machine: perh. piDAnam.
VALVE , s. kapAwaH, kapAwayuktadvAraM, piDAnaM, sapiDAnadvAraM.
Vampire, s. BUtaH, pretaH, piSAcaH.
VAMPIRE: I A ghost:(1) BUtaH;(2) pretaH. II An extortioner:(1) nizkarzaka (f. rzikA); (2) cUzaka (f. zikA).III A bat: maNgArI.
VAMPIRE , s. rAkzasaH, piSAcaH. See DEMON.
Van, s. (senA-)muKaM, agraBAgaH, agraM, mUrDan m., nAsIraM, Siras n.; ‘in the v(an)’ agre, purastAt, agrataH. 2 yAnaM; See Cart; ‘v(an)-guard’ agrAnIkaM, senAmuKaM, nAsIracarAH (pl.).
VAN: I Front: q. v.: muKam.II Car: q. v.: yAnam.
VAN , s. (Of an army, &c.) sanAmuKa, DvajinImuKaM, senAgraM, raRamUrdDA m. (n), samaramUrdDA m., nAsIraM, DAraH, Siras n.; ‘in the van,’ senA- muKe, agratas, agre, purastAta, puratas.
VAN-GUARD , s. senApuraHsaraM, agresarasEnyAH m. pl., agragasEnyAH.
VANDALISM: bArbarikatvam, -tA: v. Also cruelty, ferocity.
Vane, s. vAyugatidarSi yaMtraM.
VANE: vAyudarSanI and sim. comp. s.
VANE , s. vAyavIdiSAlakzaRaM, vAyulakzaRaM, vAyuDvajaH.
VANGUARD: (1) agrAnIkam;(2) nAsIracarAH, (m. p.);(3) senAmuKam, etc.
Vanish, v. i. tiroBU 1 P, tiroDA-aMtarDA- pass.; See Dlsappear. 2 vi-naS 4 P, pra-vi-lI 4 A.
VANISH: (1) naSyati, vi- (naS, c. 4.): v. To disappear;(2) palAyate (ay, c. 1. = fly), so long this account will not v.: tAvadidamAKyAnaM na palAyizyate, H. iv.
To VANISH , v. n. antarDA in pass., tiroBU. See To DISAPPEAR.
VANISHED , p. p. antarhitaH -tA -taM, nazwaH -zwA -zwaM. See DISAPPEARED.
VANITY: (1) vfTABimAnaH;(2) miTyABimAnitA; and sim. comp. s.

VANITY , s. (Emptiness, fruitlessness) SUnyatA, riktatA, niHsAratA vyarTatA, nirarTakatA, vEyarTyaM, moGatA; ‘music, dancing, and such like vanity,’ tUryyavAditranftyAdi asatkAryyaM. — (Conceit) ahaNkAraH, AtmABimAnaM, aBimAnaM, ahammAnaM, ahammatiH f., mAnaM, garvvaH, see CONCEIT.
Vanquish, v. t. parAji 1 A, parABU 1 P, vaSaM nI 1 P; See Humble, Subdue. [Vanquish]er, s. jetf m.
VANQUISH: parAjayate (ji, c. 1.): v. To defeat, conquer.
To VANQUISH , v. a. ji (c. 1. jayati, jetuM). See To CONQUER.
VANQUISHER: jetf (f. trI): v. Victor.
Vantage, [Vantage]-ground, s. agraBUmi f. 2 utkarzaH, SrezWapadaM.
VANTAGE, VANTAGE GROUND: agraBUmiH: v. Also superiority.
Vapid, a. virasa, nIrasa, rasahIna.
VAPID: (1) virasa (f. sA);(2) nIrasa (f. sA); (3) rasahIna (f. nA).
VAPID , a. virasaH -sA -saM, nIrasaH &c., nissAraH &c. See FLAT.
VAPOROUS, VAPOURY: I Lit.: bAzpamaya (f. yI). II Fig.: asAra (f. rA).
VAPOROUS , VAPORY, a. vAzparUpaH -pA -paM, vAzpamayaH -yI -yaM.
Vapour, s. bAzpaH, DUmaH; ‘v(apour) of the sky’ KabAzpaH, aBraM; ‘v(apour)-bath’ uzRasvedaH. v. i. vi-, katT 1 A; See Boast. [Vapour]ous, [Vapour]y, a. bAzpamaya (yI f.), bAzparUpa. 2 asAra, niHsAra.
VAPOUR: I Subs.: bAzpaH.II Verb: vikatTate (tT, c. 1.): v. To break.
VAPOUR , s. vAzpaH, svedaH, DUmaH -mikA, PenaH -natA, KavAzpaH; ‘hot vapour,’ uzRavAzpaH; ‘sultry vapour,’ mfgatfzRA, see MIRAGE; ‘vapour-bath,’ upmasvedaH, uzRasvedaH.
To VAPOUR , v. n. vikatT (c. 1. -katTate -tTituM). See To BOAST, BULLY.
VARIABLE: (1) asTira (f. rA): v. Inconstant; (2) caYcala (f. lA): v. Fickle;(3) parivartana- SIla (f. lA = changeable).
VARIABLE , a. asTiraH -rA -raM, anavasTaH -sTA -sTaM, caYcalaH -lA -laM, vizamaH -mA -maM, anityaH &c., anavasTAnaH &c. See INCONSTANT.
VARIABLENESS: (1) asTEryam: v. Inconstancy; (2) caYcalatAH v. Fickleness;(3) parivartana- SIlatvam (= changeableness).
VARIABLENESS , s. asTiratA, vEzamyaM, vizamatA, cAYcalyaM, vErUpyaM.
VARIANCE: BedaH: v. Difference, dissension.
VARIANCE , s. BedaH, dvEDaM, viroDaH, vEmanasyaM, see DIFFERENCE, s.; ‘at variance,’ parasparavirudDaH -dDA -dDaM, vipratipannaH -nnA -nnaM, vimataH &c.
VARIATION: parivfttiH: v. Change.
VARIATION , s. BedaH, parivfttiH f., vikAraH, anyaTAtvaM. See CHANGE.
VARIED: viviDavizayaka (f. kA): v. Various.

Variegate, v. t. citr 10, citrIkf 8 U, karburIkf, SabalIkf; kalmAzayati (D.). [Variegat]ed, a. citra, karbura, karburita, ki(ka)rmIra, kirmIrita, Sabala, kalmAza, kalmAzita, eta, SAra; ‘v(ariegated) colour’ karburaH, kirmIraH, SabalaH.

VARIEGATE: (1) citrayati (nomi.);(2) citrI- karoti;(3) karvurIkaroti;(4) SabalIkaroti, V. d: (1) citra (f. trA);(2) citravicitra (f. trA); (3) kavura (f. rA) or karvurita (f. tA), v. d like the dove: kapotakarvura (f. rA), Ku. iv. 27.;(4) kirmIra (f. rA) or kirmIrita (f. tA), v. d with planets: grAhOGakirmIrita (f. tA), N. xxii. 18.: (5) Sabala (f. lA), the v. d sky: SabalaM vihAyaH, Vi. vii. 26.;(6) kambara (f. rAH rare).

VEDA , s. vedaH. This is the name given to the four most ancient sacred books of the Hindūs, viz. the Ṛich or Ṛig-veda fgvedaH, the Yajus or Yajurveda yajurvedaH, the Sāman or sAmavedaH, and the Atharvan or Atharva-veda aTarvavedaH. Of these the Ṛig-veda is the most celebrated. It consists of metrical hymns or prayers termed sūktas or mantras, each stanza of which is called a ṛch, ad- dressed chiefly to the gods of the elements, Fire, Air, the Sun, &c., and ascribed to different holy authors or Ṛiṣis. The Yajurveda consists principally of prayers and invo- cations applicable to the consecration of the utensils and materials of sacrificial worship. It is divided into two parts, the white and black, the former of which is attri- buted to the saint Yājnavalkya, and the latter to Tittiri. The Sama-veda is little else than a recast of the Ṛig- veda, being made up of many of the same hymns, broken into parts and arranged anew for the purpose of being chanted during various expiatory ceremonies. The Atharva-veda has little in common with the other three in its character or style. Its language indicates a different and later era, and it may therefore be regarded as a supplement to the three others. Hence it is that many passages are found in Sanskrit writings which limit the number of Vedas to three. Each of the Vedas consists of two distinct component parts, viz. the Mantra [Page827-b+ 51] portion, and the Brāhmaṇa portion. The Mantra por- tion is a collection or Sanhitā of sūktas, or hymns as above described, the composition of which is supposed to have taken place about twelve or thirteen centuries B. C.; the Brāhmaṇa portion is a collection of rules for the repetition of the Mantras at certain particular cere- monies, with directions for the performance of such ceremonies, and illustrative remarks explanatory of their origin. This portion of the Vedas is supposed to have been composed about seven or eight centuries B. C. The Vedas were collected and arranged into books and chapters by the sage Kṛṣnadvaipayana, surnamed Vyāsa, who is supposed to have lived in the eleventh century after Christ; see under PURĀNA. The Vedas collectively are often called SrutiH f. or AmnAyaH, and a Brāhman conversant with them SrotriyaH or SrutijYaH. — (The three Vedas) vedatrayaM -yI, trayI; ‘duty enjoined by them,’ trayIDarmmaH. — (The four Vedas) caturvedaM; ‘one who is conver- sant with them,’ caturvidyaH, caturvedaH, cAturvEdyaH. Ventilate, v. t. vIj 10; See Fan. 2 pracar c., pra-sf c. [Ventilat]ed, a. pravAta, vAyuvyApta; ‘a bed in a v(entilated) place’ pravAtaSayanaM (M. 4). [Ventilat]or, s. vIjanaM, vyajanaM.
VENTILATE: I To fan.: q. v.: vIjayati (vIj, c. 10.).II To cause air to pass: the house is well v. d: vAyuprasArabahulaM gfham.III To circu- -late: pracArayati (c. of car).
To VENTILATE , v. a. (Fan) vIj, upavIj, see To FAN. — (Cause the air to pass through) vAyuvyApyaM -pyAM kf, vAyuvyAptaM -ptAM kf.
VENTILATED , p. p. vAyuvyAptaH -ptA -ptaM, upavIjitaH &c., anuvIjitaH &c.
VENTILATION: I Lit.: vAyuprasAraH and sim. comp. s.II Fig.: pracAraH.
VENTILATOR: I A machine: vAyuprasAriRI (?). II Publisher: pracAraka (f. rikA).
VENTILATOR , s. vAyuyantraM, vyajanaM, duzwavAyUtkzepakayantraM.
Ventral, a. udara in comp.
VENTRAL , a. OdarikaH -kI -kaM, udarakaH -kA -kaM, kOkzaH -kzI -kzaM.
Ventricle, s. koSaH-zaH, dvAraM.
VENTRICLE: kozaH (SaH); fourth v.: caturTakoSaH.
VENTRICLE , s. ranDraM, dvAraM, kozWaH, kozaH, koSaH, raktakozaH.
VENTRILOQUISM: (1) gAruqavARI;(2) udaravAdaH.
VENTRILOQUISM , s. gAruqavARI, EndrajAlikavARI, udaravAdaH.
Ventriloquist, s. gAruqavAdin m. Ventriloquism, s. gAruqavAdaH.
VENTRILOQUIST: gAruqavAdin (f. nI) and sim. comp. s.
VENTRILOQUIST , s. udaravAdI m. (n), gAruqavARIyuktaH.

details.body: Venture, s. sAhasaM, sAhasakriyA. 2 saMkawa, saMSayaH; See Danger. v. i. saMSaye nikzip 6 P. 2 utsah 1 A, sAhasaM kf 8 U, Dfz 5 P; ‘we cannot v(enture) to state this’ iti kaTanarUpaM sAhasaM kartuM na SaknumaH, iti kaTayituM notsahAmahe; ‘nothing v(enture), nothing gain’ sAhase SrIH prativasati. [Ventur]ous, [Venture]some, a. sAhasika (kI f.) sAhasabudDi.
VENTURE (subs.): I Bold undertaking: sAhasam.II Risk: saNkawam. Ph.: at a venture: sahasA: v. Suddenly.
VENTURE: I To risk: q. v.II To attempt: q. v. Ph.: nothing v. nothing gain: udyamena hi siDyanti kAryARi na manoraTEH, H. 36.
VENTURE , s. see HAZARD, RISK; ‘at a venture,’ dEvAt.
VENTURESOME, VENTUROUS: sAhasika (f. kI): v. Bold, dangerous.
VENTURESOME , a. sAhasikaH -kI -kaM, sAhasabudDiH &c. See DARING, a.
VENUE: sTAnam: v. Place.
Venus, s. SukraH, BArgavaH, kaviH, uSanas m., kAvyaH, dEtyaguruH.

VENUS , s. (In mythology) ratiH f., see RATI. — (The planet) SukraH, uSanAH m. (s), BfguH m., BArgavaH, kaviH m., kAvyaH, SvetaH, SvetaraTaH, boqaSAMSaH m., maGABavaH, AsPujit m., dEtyaguruH m. Śukra, the [Page828-b+ 51] egentregent of the planet Venus, is fabled as the son of Bhṛgu, and preceptor of the Daityas or demons.
Veracious, a. satyavAc, satyagir, satya-vAdin, satyaSIla. Veracity, s. satyavA-ditvaM, satyaSIlatA.
VERACIOUS: (1) satyavAdin (f. nI);(2) satyavAc (mfn.);(3) satyagir (mfn.);(4) satyaSIla (f. lA), etc.

VERACIOUS , a. satyavAdI -dinI -di (n), satyavAk m. f. n. (c), satya- vaktA -ktrI -ktf (ktf), satyaBAzI &c., ftavAk m. f. n., satyavacAH -cAH -caH (s), satyavadanaSIlaH -lA -laM, satyaSIlaH -lA -laM, satyABiDAyI &c., avitaTavAdI &c., pUtavAk m. f. n., satyagIH -gIH -giH (r), satyasanDaH -nDA -nDaM.
VERACITY: (1) satyavAditvam-, tA;(2) satyaBAzaRam; etc.
VERACITY , s. satyavAditvaM, satyavaktftvaM, satyABiDAnaM, satyaBAzaRaM, satyaM, satya- SIlatA, satyatA, satyavadyaM, satyA.
VERANDA , s. varaRqaH -RqakaH, nizkASaH, AvarakaH. See PORTICO.
VERANDAH: (1) varaRqaH;(2) nizkASaH.

Verb, s. kriyA, -padaM. [Verb]al, a. SAbdika (kI f.), SAbda (bdI f.), SabdarUpa. 2 (Oral) vAcika-vAcanika- (kI f.); (vAcika-midAnIM SrotumicCAmi Mu. 5). [Verb]ally, adv. vAcA. 2 SabdataH, yaTASabdaM [Verb]atim, adv. yaTAvyAhftaM, padAnupadaM, SabdaSaH, yaTA-SabdaM. [Verb]ose, a. vAgbahula, ativistIrRa; See Prolix. [Verb]osity, [Verb]iage, s. vAgvistaraH, vAkprapaMcaH, vAgupacayaH.
VERB: (1) DAtuH (verbal root), intransitive v.: akarmako DAtuH, Kaṇada; although the v. ‘to do’ is transitive: yadyapi kfDAtoH sakarmatvamastyeva;(2) kriyA (conjugated).
VERB , s. kriyA, kriyApadaM; ‘form of a verb,’ kriyArUpaM, DAturUpaM, AKyAtaM; ‘root of a verb,’ DAtuH m.; ‘subject of one,’ kri- yASrayaH; ‘table or list of verbs,’ DAtupAWaH.

VERBAL: I Oral:(1) vAcika (f. kI), now I wish to hear the v. message: vAcikamidAnIM Srotu- micCAmi, Mu. v.;(2) vAcanika (f. kI).II Of words:(1) by comp.;(2) SAbdika (f. kI);(3) SAbda (f. bdI).III Literal: q. v.: padAnupadika (f. kI ?).

VERBAL , a. (Expressed in words) vAcikaH -kI -kaM, vAcanikaH -kI -kaM, vAcakaH -kA -kaM, SabdadvArakaH &c. — (Consisting in words, relating to words) SAbdaH -bdI -bdaM, SAbdikaH -kI -kaM, SabdarUpaH -pA -paM, SabdasambanDI &c. — (Literal) padAnupadikaH -kI -kaM, samapadaH -dA -daM, SabdarUpaH -pA -paM, see LITERAL. — (In grammar) kriyA- vAcakaH -kA -kaM, DAtusADitaH -tA -taM.
VERBALLY: I Orally: vAcA, and sim. expr. s. II Lit.: padAnupadam.
VERBALLY , adv. SabdadvArA -reRa, Sabdatas, yaTASabdaM.
VERBATIM: (1) padAnupadam;(2) yaTAvyAhftam; etc.
VERBATIM , adv. SabdaSas, Sabdatas, akzaraSas, yaTASabdaM.
VERBENA: suganDitfRaviSezaH.
VERBENA , s. (Kind of grass) darBaH.
VERBIAGE, VERBOSITY: (1) vAgvistAraH;(2) vAkprapaYcaH;(3) BUyasI vAk, Si. ii. 23.; etc.
VERBOSE: (1) vAgbahula (f. lA);(2) vistIrRa (f. rRA = frolics).
VERBOSE , a. bahuSabdakaH -kA -kaM, bahuvAkyaH -kyA -kyaM, atiSayoktivi- SizwaH -zwA -zwaM, ativistIrRaH &c., see PROLIX.
VERBOSITY , VERBIAGE, s. SabdavistAraH, bahuSabdatvaM, atiSayoktiH f., Sabda- bAhulyaM, bahuBAzitA, SabdADikyaM.
Verdant, a. harita, SAdvala.
VERDANT: (1) harita (f. tA): v. Green;(2) SAdvala (f. lA): v. Grassy.
VERDANT , a. haritaH -tA -riRI -taM, SAdaharitaH &c., SAqvalaH -lA -laM, amlAnaH &c.; ‘to become so,’ harita (nom. haritAyate).
Verdict, s. nirRayaH; vicAraH; daMqanirRayaH.
VERDICT: nirRayaH: Decision, opinion.
VERDICT , s. nirRayapAdaH, nirRayaH, daRqanirRayaH. See SENTENCE.
Verdigris, s. tAmrakiwwaM-malaM, kalaMkaH.
VERDIGRIS: tAmrakiwwam, tAmramalam, etc.
VERDIGRIS , s. kalaNkaH, tAmrakalaNkaH, tAmramalaM, tAmrakiwwaM.
Verdure, s. haritatvaM, hArityaM; SAdaH, SAdva-latA; ‘clothed in fresh v(erdure) of sprouts’ navaharitasasyAMkuravatI.
VERDURE: (1) SAdaH;(2) SAdvalatAH v. of = ver- -dant: q. v.
VERDURE , s. SAdaH, navaSAdaH, haritaSAdaH, haritatvaM, amlAniH f.

Verge, s. prAMtaH, paryaMtaH, DArA; ‘on the v(erge) of’ unmuKa (KI f.) Asasna in comp.; ‘on the v(erge) of ruin’ vinASonmuKa, Asa-nnalaya. 2 daMqaH, yazwi f. v. i. ava-, laMb 1 A; by (s.); ‘is v(erg)ing on ruin’ Asanna-nASo vartate; ‘when it was v(erg)ing towards sunset’ pariRataprAye ahani ‘v(erg)ing on 18’ azwAvaSavarzadeSIya; See Border. [Verg]er, s. daMqin m., daMqa-vetra-DaraH.
VERGE (subs.): I Border, edge: prAntaH.II Rod: daRqaH. Ph.: on the v. of ruin: patano- nmuKa (f. KI): v. About.
VERGE (v.): I To incline, slope: q. v.: lambate (lamb, c. 1.).II Fig.: v. ing on middle age: maDyamopAnte vayasi vartamAnayoH, Va.
VERGE , s. (Rod) daRqaH. — (Brink) prAntaH, DArA, see BRINK.
VERGER: (1) daRqin (m.);(2) daRqaDaraH;(3) vetrin (m.).
VERGER , s. daRqI m. (n), daRqaDaraH. See MACE-BEARER.
VERIFICATION: (1) by verb;(2) samarTanam, nA : v. Also examination.
VERIFICATION , s. satyAkftiH f., satyAkaraRaM, satyaNkftiH f., satyaNkAraH, satyA- panaM, satyaNkaraRaM, nirRetftvaM, nirRAyanaM.
Verify, v. t. pramARIkf 8 U, pramARayati (D.), samarT 10, satyAkf, satyApayati (D.), nirRI 1 P. [Verif]ication, s. satyApanaM, satyAkAraH.
VERIFY: (1) pramARayati (nomi.);(2) samarTayati (nomi.), I would v. this proverb...: iti lokavAdaM samarTayeyam, D. vi.: v. Also to prove, estab- -lish.
To VERIFY , v. a. satyAkf, satyaNkf, satyIkf, satya (nom. caus. satyApa- yati -yituM), nirRI, niSci, nirRayaM kf.
Verily, adv. satyaM, nUnaM, niyataM, nAma, Kalu.
VERILY: (1) satyam: v. Indeed, truly;(2) nUnam: v. Certainly.
VERILY , adv. satyaM, avaSyaM, nUnaM. See TRULY, CERTAINLY.
Verisimilitude, s. saMBavaH. 2 sAdfSyaM.
Vermes, s. (pl.) kfmayaH, kIwakAH. Vermicide, Vermifuge, a. kfmi-hara-Gna (GnI f.). Vermicular, a. kfmisadfSa (SI f.). Vermiform, a. kIwakAkfti.
VERMICULAR , a. kfmisadfSaH -SI -SaM, kfmigatisadfSaH -SI -SaM.
VERMIFUGE , a. kfmiharaH -rA -raM, kfmiGnaH -GnI -GnaM, kfmihArI -riRI &c.
VERMILION: I Lit.: sindUram.II Fig.: SoRa (f. RA): v. Red.
VERMILION (v.): sindUreRa raYjayati, aBi-, anu- (raYj, c. 10.).
VERMILION , s. sindUraM, sindUrikA, hiNgulaH, raktaM, cUrRapAradaH, suraNgaM, citrANgaM, rasagarBaH, haMsapAdaM, hasAMGriH m., kapiSIrzakaM.
Vermillion, s. siMdUraM. a. SoRa, rakta. v. t. ‘cover with v(ermillion)’ sEMdUrIkf, siMdUreRa raMj c.
Vermin, s. kfmayaH (pl.), kfmigaRaH.
VERMIN: kfmiH or kfmayaH (m. pl.).
VERMIN , s. kfmayaH m. pl., garttASritAH m. pl., vilevAsinaH m. pl., vi- leSayAH m. pl., mUzikAdikzudrajantavaH m. pl., gfhotpAtaH.
Vernacular, a. janma in comp.; ‘v(ernacular) dialects’ BAzA, prAkftaBAzA. s. janmaBAzA, mAtfBAzA.
VERNACULAR: I Adj.: janma- in comp.: v. Native, country.II Subs.:(1) mAtfBAzA; (2) BAzA (when sense is clear).
VERNACULAR , a. janmadeSIyaH -yA -yaM, svadeSIyaH &c., prAkftaH -tI -taM; ‘language,’ janmaBAzA, prAkftaBAzA.
Vernal, a. vAsaMta (tI f.) vAsaMtika (kI f.), vasaMta in comp.
VERNAL: (1) vasanta- in comp.;(2) vAsanta (f. ntI);(3) vAsantika (f. kI); etc.
VERNAL , a. vAsantaH -ntI -ntaM, vAsantikaH -kI -kaM, vasantajaH -jA -jaM, vasantodBavaH -vA -vaM, vasanta in comp.
Versatile, a. capala, lola, lola-mati-budDi, caMcalaH See Fickie. [Versatil]ity, s. (budDi-)cApalyaM, lOlyaM.
VERSATILE: I Unsteady: q. v.: caYcala (f. lA). II Readily applied to various subjects: of v. genius: sarvadakza (f. kzA): v. Skilful.

VERSATILE , a. capalabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, capalamatiH -tiH -ti, caYcalabudDiH [Page829-a+ 51] &c., anekabudDiH &c., capalaH -lA -laM, caYcalaH &c., anyamAnasaH -sI -saM, anyamanaskaH -skA -skaM, capalamanaskaH &c.
VERSATILITY , s. budDicApalyaM, capalabudDitvaM, capalatA.

Verse, s. kavitA, padyaM, kAvyaM; ‘syllabic v(erse)’ vfttaM; ‘blank v(erse)’ muktaprAsaH. 2 SlokaH. 3 (‘Portion of v(erse)’) caraRaH, pAdaH, padaM. Versify, v. t. padyAni rac 10 or nibaMD 9 P, kavayati (D.). [Versif]ier, s. kaviH, kavi-deSyaH. [Versif]ication, s. Sloka-padya-racanA, CaMdobaMDaH.
VERSE: I Poetry: q. v.: kabitA.II Stanza: SlokaH. Ph.: a poem of seven hundred v. s: saptaSatI.III Metrical line:(1) caraRam;(2) pAdaH;(3) padam.

VERSE , s. (Metrical composition) padyaM, kavitA, kAvyaM, Candas n., gA; ‘measured by time,’ jAtiH f.; ‘syllabic,’ vfttaM; ‘blank,’ muktaprAsaH; ‘prose and verse,’ gadyapadyaM. — (Stanza) SlokaH, gATA, rUpaM. — (Line of a stanza) pAdaH, caraRaH -RaM, padaM; ‘verse by verse,’ pAdaSas.
Versed, a. aBijYa, kuSala, nipuRa, pravIRa, supratizWita, aByaMtara, viSArada; See Skilful.
VERSED: (1) aBijYa (f. jYA): v. Knowing; (2) viSArada (f. dA): v. Proficient.
VERSED , a. aBijYaH -jYA -jYaM, nipuRaH -RA -RaM, kuSalaH -lA -laM, viSAradaH -dA -daM, nizWitaH -tA -taM, parinizWitaH &c., see SKILLED, CONVER- SANT; ‘in all subjects,’ sarvvavizayajYaH -jYA -jYaM.
VERSICLE: kzudrakavitA, and sim. comp. s.
VERSIFICATION: CandobanDaH; SlokaracanA; and sim. comp. s.
VERSIFICATION , s. SlokaracanA, padaracanA, kAvyaracanA, padayojanA, kavi- tAkaraRaM, kAvyakaraRaM, SlokatvaM.
VERSIFIER: (1) kavayitf (f. trI);(2) padyaracayitf (f. trI) and sim. comp. s.
VERSIFIER , s. SlokaracakaH, kavitAkarttA m. (rttf), BavinaH.
VERSIFY: (1) kavayati (nomi.), Bho.;(2) padyaM karoti, etc.
To VERSIFY , v. n. SlokaracanAM kf, padaracanAM kf, kavitAM kf.
Version, s. Translation, q. v. 2 pAWAMtaraM, pAWaBedaH.
VERSION: authorized v.: *parinizWitavyAvftiH: v. Translation.
VERSION , s. BAzAntaraM, see TRANSLATION. — (Variation in reading) pAWAntaraM, pAWaBedaH, pAWaH.
Vertebra, s. pfzWavaMSAsTi n. [Vertebra]te, [Vertebra]ted, a. pfzWavaMSayuta-viSizwa.
VERTEBRA: pfzWavaMSAsTi (n.); (2) mAMsasanDiH (?).
VERTEBRA , s. pfzWavaMSagranTiH m., pfzWavaMSasanDiH m., vaMSasanDiH
VERTEBRAL , a. vaMSagranTisambanDI &c., vaMSasanDisambanDI &c.
VERTEBRATED , a. pfzWAsTimAn -matI -mat, pfzWavaMSaviSizwaH &c.
VERTEBRATY,-E: (1) kaSerumat (f. tI);(2) pfzWavaMSayuta (f. tA) and sim. comp. s.
Vertex, s. SIrzaM, agraM, SiKaraM; See Top also.
VERTEX: SIrzam: v. Top, summit.
VERTEX , s. agraM, SiKA, SiKaraM, Siras n., tuNgaH.
Vertical, a. UrDva-upari-tana (nI f.), laMba-rUpa. [Vertical]ly, adv. aDomuKaM, UrDvADaraM.
VERTICAL: I Upper: q. v.: UrDvatana (f. nI). II Perpendicular: q. v. Ph.: v. circle: dfgvfttam; v. parallax: dfglambanam; prime v.: sama- maRqalam, Su.

VERTICAL , a. UrdDvADaraH -rA -raM, see PERPENDICULAR. — (In the zenith) svamaDyasTaH -sTA -sTaM. — (Vertical circle, in astronomy) dfNmaRqalaM; ‘passing through nonagesimal point,’ dfkkzepavfttaM; ‘prime vertical,’ samamaRqalaM, pfrvvAparavfttaM.
VERTICALLY: (1) aDomuKam;(2) avANmuKam: v. Also perpendicularly.
VERTICALLY , adv. UrdDvADaraM, UrdDvADararUpeRa, see PERPENDICULARLY; ‘he places the tube vertically in the vessel,’ talam upari- viDAya nAlaM pAtre sTApayati.
Vertigo, s. BramaraM; See Giddiness.
VERTIGO: Bramaram: v. Dizziness.
VERTIGO , s. BramaraM. See GIDDINESS, DIZZINESS.
Verve, s. utsAhaH, AveSaH.

Very, adv. ati-su pr., sAtiSayaM, atIva, BUri, ni-su-tarAM, atyaMtaM; See Exceedingly; ‘v(ery) deceitful’ BUrimAya a.; ex. by demonstrative pron. with eva; ‘the v(ery) hills’ ta eva girayaH; ‘this v(ery) day’ adyEva. 2 satya, taTya. 3 mAtraM in comp., kevala.

VERY (adj.): I Real, actual: q. v.: expr. by adv. satyam etc.II Same: q. v., he is the v. man: ayaM saH.III Emphatic: expr. with eva, it is the v. same forest: etattadeva hi vanam, U. ii. 22.; these are the v. same mountains: ete ta eva girayaH, U. ii. 23.; this very day: adyEva, Ve. iv. 1.

VERY (adv.): (1) ati- in comp., v. scarce: atidurlaBa (f. BA);(2) su- in comp. (= good), v. many (= good many): subahu (mfn.); v. far, (= good distance): sudUram; v. hot (= well heated): sutapta (f. ptA);(3) by comp. or super., v. heavy rain: baMhIyasI vfzwiH, Si. iii. 6.; v. quick: kzepIyas, Vi. v. 15.; v. swift: drutatara (f. rA), Si. xi. 8.; v. big: vipulatara (f. rA), Si. xi. 5.: v. Also exceeding, extremely.

VERY , a. (Real) satyaH -tyA -tyaM, vAstavaH -vI -vaM; ‘in very deed,’ satyameva; ‘the very one,’ ayaM viSezaH; ‘I, that very person,’ so'ham. — (Mere) SudDaH -dDA -dDaM, mAtra in comp.; ‘the very birth of a Brāhman,’ brAhmaRajanmamAtraM. — (Emphatic) expressed by eva; as, ‘from that very moment,’ tatkzaRAdeva; ‘this very day,’ adyEva.

VERY , adv. ati or su or atiSaya prefixed, atIva, atiSayena, atyantaM, BUri, suzWu, see EXTREMELY, EXCEEDINGLY; ‘very angry,’ atyamarzI -rziRI &c., atikroDI &c.; ‘very many,’ subahuH -huH -hu, ‘very far,’ sudUraH -rA -raM; ‘very glorious,’ amitatejAH -jAH -jaH (s); ‘very deceitful,’ anantamAyI &c.; ‘love is very suspicious,’ snehaH param ASaNkate; ‘very well,’ paramaM, vAQaM; ‘very true,’ evameva, paramaM.
Vesicle, s. tvak-carma-sPowaH.
VESICLE: perh. kozakaH; kzudrakozaH; etc.
VESICLE , s. kzudrasPowaH, tvaksPowakaH, carmmasPowaH.
VESICULAR: I Lit.: kozakamaya (f. yI).II Hollow: q. v.
Vesper, s. saMDyA, saMDyopAsanaM.
VESPER: I Evening: q. v.: sanDyA.II Evening star: sAyantanI tArA.
VESPERS , s. sAyampUjA, sAyamBajanaM, sanDyApUjA, sanDyABajanaM.
VESPERTINE , a. sAyaNkAlikaH -kI -kaM, sAyantanaH &c. See EVENING, a.
Vessel, s. pAtraM, BAjanaM, BAMqaM, ADAraH. 2 potaH, samudrayAnaM, jalayAnaM, vahitraM, nOH. 3 nAqI; See Vein.
VESSEL: I A receptacle:(1) pAtram;(2) BAjanam.II A ship: q. v.: yAnapAtram.III Of the body: nAqiH (qI): v. Vein, etc.

VESSEL , s. (Utensil for holding, as a pot, cup, &c.) pAtraM, BAjanaM, BARqaM, amatraM, ADAraH, DArakaH; ‘drinking vessel,’ pAnapAtraM; ‘for holding water,’ udakapAtraM, jalapAtraM, GawaH, kalaSaH. — (Vessel of the body, as a vein, &c.) SirA, nAqiH -qI f., nAliH -lI, DamanI, vAhinI, see TUBE. — (Boat, ship) nOH f., nOkA, potaH, vahinI, vahitraM, taraRI, jalayAnaM, vohitTaM.

Vest, s. vastraM, veSaH-zaH, vasanaM. v. t. vez c., pari-DA c.; See Dress. [Vest]ed, a. (in) vyavasTita; ‘are warlike qualities v(ested) (in any one)’ kiM vyavasTitavizayAH kzAtraDarmA iti (U. 5). 2 aDIna, Ayatta. Vestment, Vesture, s. vAsas n., vastraM; Dress.

VISHNU , s. vizRuH. The second person of the Hindū triad, and the most celebrated and popular of all the Indian deities. He is the personification of the preserving power, and became incarnate in nine different forms, for the preservation of mankind in various emergencies. Before the creation of the universe, and after its tem- porary annihilation, he is supposed to sleep on the waters, floating on the serpent Śeṣa, and is then identi- fied with Nārāyana. Brahmā, the creator, is fabled to spring at that time from a lotus which grows from his navel, whilst thus asleep. Viṣṇu's wife is called Lak- ṣmī, and the vehicle on which he rides, Garuḍa. See LAKSHMI, GARUḌA. His ten avatārs or incarnations are: 1. The Matsya, or Fish. In this avatār Viṣṇu descended in the form of a fish to save the pious king Satyavrata, who with the seven Ṛiṣis and their wives had taken refuge in the ark to escape the deluge which then destroyed the earth. 2. The Kūrma, or Tortoise. In this he descended in the form of a tortoise, for the pur- pose of restoring to man some of the comforts lost dur- ing the flood. To this end he stationed himself at the bottom of the ocean, and allowed the point of the great mountain Mandara to be placed upon his back, which served as a hard axis, whereon the gods and demons, [Page831-b+ 51] with the serpent Vāsuki twisted round the mountain for a rope, churned the waters for the recovery of the amṛta or nectar, and fourteen other sacred things, see OCEAN. 3. The Varāha, or Boar. In this he descended in the form of a boar to rescue the earth from the power of a demon called ‘golden-eyed,’ Hiraṇyākṣa. This demon had seized on the earth and carried it with him into the depths of the ocean. Viṣṇu dived into the abyss, and, after a contest of a thousand years, slew the monster. 4. The Narasinha, or Man-lion. In this monstrous shape of a creature half-man, half-lion, Viṣṇu delivered the earth from the tyranny of an insolent demon called Hiraṇyakaśipu. 5. Vāmana, or Dwarf. This avatār happened in the second age of the Hindūs or Tretā yug, the four preceding are said to have occurred in the first or Satya yug; the object of this avatar was to trick Bali out of the dominion of the three worlds. Assuming the form of a wretched dwarf he appeared before the king, and asked, as a boon, as much land as he could pace in three steps. VISIT , s. aByAgamaH -manaM, aBigamaH, darSanayAtrA, samAyaH.

VISWAKARMA , s. (Architect or artist of the gods) viSvakarmmA m. (n), devatvazwA m. (zwf), devavardDakiH m., tvazwA m., devaSilpI m.

VITALITY , s. jIvaSaktiH f., jIvanaSaktiH f., prARaSaktiH f., jIvaH, prARaH, ojas n., cetanA, cEtanyaM, sajIvatvaM, prARakarmma n.

VITALS , s. pl. marmmARi n. pl., marmmasTAnaM, marmmasTalaM.

VITIATION , s. dUpaRaM, pAMsanaM, dfzwatA. See CORRUPTION.

VITRIFY: kAcIkaroti (?).

Vitrious, a. kAcaja, kAcABa, kAcamaya (yI f.). Vitrify, v. t. kAcasAtkf 8 U.
VITUPERATE: Akzipati (kzip, c. 6.): v. To censure, revile.
VITUPERATION: AkzepaH: v. Censure, reproach.

VIVA-VOCE , muKatas, muKadvArA, muKadvAreRa.
Vivacious, a. praPulla, sotsAha, satejas. [Vivacious]ness, Vivacity, s. utsAhaH; teja-svitA, praPullatA, ullAsaH.

VIVACIOUSLY: (1) praPullaB: v. Cheerfully;(2) tejasA (= vigorously).
VIVACIOUSNESS, VIVACITY: (1) praPullatA (= cheer- -fulness);(2) tejasvitA (= vigorousness).
VIVACITY , s. tejas n., ullasatA, ullAsaH. See LIVELINESS.
Vivid, a. suspazwa, viSada, parisPuwa.
VIVID: (1) vicitra (f. trA = picturesque);(2) viSada (f. dA = clear).

To VIVIFY , v. a. jIv (c. 10. jIvayati -yituM), saMjIv. See To ANIMATE.
Viviparous, a. jarAyuja, jIvaja. 2 saceta-napraja.
VIVIPAROUS: (1) jarAyujaH (jA, jaM), Sr.;(2) jIvajaH (jA, jaM), Up.
VIVIPAROUS , a. sacetanaprasUH f., sacetanaprajA. — (Born from the womb) jarAyujaH -jA -jaM.

VIXEN , s. karkaSA, caRqI, kroDanA. See SCOLD.
VIXENISH: (1) KiNKirI;(2) KiKivaDUH; etc.
VIZIER , s. mantrI m. (n), amAtyaH. See MINISTER.
Vocable, s. SabdaH, vAkyaM, vacanaM.

VOCABLE , s. SabdaH, vAkyaM, vacanaM, vAcakaH. See WORD.
Vocabulary, s. aBiDAnaM, koSaH, SabdArRavaH, SabdasaMgrahaH-koSaH.
VOCABULARY: (1) aBiDAnam;(2) kozaH;(3) SabdArRavaH.
VOCABULARY , s. SabdakozaH, SabdasaMgrahaH, kozaH. See LEXICON.
Vocal, a. vAcika (kI f.), vANmaya (yI f.), vAgjAta. 2 vARIyukta, vAgviSizwa. 3 susvara, maDuraH ‘v(ocal) music’ kaMWagItaM.
VOCAL: I Lit.:(1) vAgviSizwa (f. zwA) and sim. comp. s (= endowed with voice);(2) vAcika (f. kI = oral: q. v.).II Sonorous: q. v.
VOCAL , a. (Having a voice) vAgyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, vARIyuktaH &c. savAk m. f. n. (c), vARIviSizwaH &c. — (Uttered by the voice) vAcikaH -kA -kaM, vARIjAtaH -tA -taM, vAgjAtaH &c.
Vocation, s. vftti f., vyavasAyaH, niyogaH, vyApAraH.
VOCATION: (1) vfttiH;(2) vyavasAyaH;(3) karman (n.): v. Business.
VOCATION , s. vfttiH f., vyApAraH, vyavasAyaH, karmma n. See BUSINESS.
Vocative, s. saMboDanaM, saMbudDi f.
VOCATIVE: (1) samboDanam;(2) sambudDiH.
VOCATIVE , s. (Case in grammar) samboDanaM, sambudDiH f., AmantraRaM, azwamI viBaktiH.
Vociferate, v. i. uccEH AkraMd 1 P, utkruS 1 P, ud-Guz 10. [Vociferat]ion, s. AkroSaH, ud-GozaH. Vociferous, a. mahASabda, sako-lAhala, udGozaRa. [Vociferous]ly, adv. mahASabdena, udGozeRa.
VOCIFERATE: utkroSati (kruS, c. 1.): v. To shout, cry out.
To VOCIFERATE , v. n. uccEr Guz or utkruS. See To CLAMOUR, CRY.
VOCIFERATION: utkroSaH: v. Noise, shout.
VOCIFERATION , s. GozaRaM -RA, utkroSaH. See EXCLAMATION.
VOCIFEROUS: mahASabda (f. bdA) and sim. comp. s.: v. Noisy, tumultuous.
VOCIFEROUS , a. mahAGozaH -zA -zaM, udGozaRaH &c. See CLAMOROUS.
VOCIFEROUSLY: mahASabdena: v. Noisily, tum- -ultuously.
Vogue, s. vyavahAraH, pravftti f., pracAraH, rIti f., kzuRRA padDatiH; ‘it is not in v(ogue) here’ atra nedfSo vyavahAraH; ‘being long in v(ogue)’ cirapravftta.

VOGUE , s. pracAraH, lokapracAraH, vyavahAraH, pracaraH, rItiH f.

Voice, s. svaraH, svanaH, nAdaH, SabdaH, vARI, vacanaM, vAc f., kaMWaDvaniH-ravaH. 2 mataM, aBiprAyaH; ‘with one v(oice)’ ekacittIBUya, Ekama-tyena; ‘cracked v(oice)’ BagnasvaraH; ‘active v(oice)’ kartfvAcyaM; ‘passive v(oice)’ karmavAcyaM; ‘neuter v(oice)’ BAvavAcyaM.

(c), kaRWaravaH, vacanaM, vacas n., uktiH f., vyAhAraH, vyAhftiH f., BAzitaM, lapitaM, kaRWaDvaniH m.; ‘having a sweet voice,’ maDurasvaraH -rA -raM; ‘having an unpleasant voice,’ asOmyasvaraH -rA -raM, asvaraH &c.; ‘having the voice of a lion,’ siMhanAdaH -dA -daM; ‘having a cracked voice,’ BagnasvaraH &c.; ‘change of voice,’ svaraBedaH, svaravikAraH. — (In grammar) vAcyaM, padaM; ‘active voice,’ karttfvAcyaM, parasmEpadaM; ‘middle,’ AtmanepadaM; ‘passive,’ karmaRivAcyaM, BAvavAcyaM.

VOID , a. (Empty) SUnyaH -nyA -nyaM, riktaH -ktA -ktaM, SUnyAkAraH -rA -raM, see EMPTY. — (Null) nirarTakaH -kA -kaM, see NULL. — (Devoid) hInaH -nA -naM, SUnyaH &c., see DEVOID, DESTITUTE.
VOID , s. SUnyaM, riktaM, SUnyatA. See VACUUM.
To VOID , v. a. uccar, utsfj, utsargaM kf, had (c. 1. hadati -dituM), gu (c. 6. guvati -vituM). See To EVACUATE, EXCREMENT, &c.
VOIDABLE: perh. nirasanIya (f. yA), vivarjanIya (f. yA), etc.
VOIDED , p. p. uccaritaH -tA -taM, gUnaH -nA -naM, hannaH -nnA -nnaM.
Volatile, a. vAyupariRAmaSIla. 2 caMcala, lola; See Fickle. [Volatil]ity, s. cApalyaM, cAMcalyaM.

VOLATILITY: I Lit.: vAyupariRAmaSIlatA.II Fickleness: caYcalatA.
VOLATILITY , s. caYcalatA, cAYcalyaM, capalatA, cApalyaM, asTiratA.
VOLCANIC , a. jvAlAmuKIsambanDI -nDinI &c., adrivahnisambanDI &c.

VOLLEY , s. varzaH, vfzwiH f., pAtaH; ‘of stones,’ SilAvarzaH, aSmavarzaH.
VOLUBILITY: I Lit.: caYcalatA.II Fluency: q. v.: vAcAlatA.

VOLUBLE: I Lit.: caYcala (f. lA).II Fluent: q. v.: vAcAla (f. lA), Me. ii. 33. Ph.: having v. tongue: capalajihva (f. hvA).
VOLUBLE , a. vAkcapalaH -lA -laM, capalajihvaH &c., see FLUENT, GLIB.
Volume, s. KaMqaH-qaM, BAgaH, pustakaM (when the sense is clear). 2 aMtagartaMaMtargataM GanaPalaM. 3 Avali-lI f., pawalaM, rASiH, saMhati f. Voluminous, a. vistIrRa, bahupustaka.

Voracious, a. Gasmara, gfDnu, atilolupa, Odarika (kI f.); See Gluttonous.

VORACIOUSNESS, VORACITY: (1) GasmaratA;(2) OdarikatA: v. Also greediness, gluttony.
Vortex, s. Brami f., AvartaH.
VORTEX: (1) AvartaH;(2) AvartanI;(3) BramiH.
VORTEX , s. AvarttaH -rttikA, BramaH. See EDDY, WHIRLPOOL.
Votary, s. BaktaH, upAsakaH, pUjakaH; ASritaH.
VOTARY: (1) Bakta (f. ktA);(2) by comp., v. ies of Śiva: SEvAH: v. Also worshipper.
VOTARY , s. BaktaH, BaktimAn m. (t), BaktilaH, sevakaH, upAsakaH, AsaktaH, parAyaRaH, ASritaH; ‘of Kṛṣṇa,’ kfzRASritaH, kfzRaMSritaH.
Vote, s. saMmati f., saMmataM. v. t. saMmatiM-anumodanaM-dA 3 U, mataM prakAS c.; saMmatipUrvaM vf 5 U or niyuj 7 A, 10 or dA.
VOTE: (subs.): no equiv.: sammatiH (= appro- -val) may be used.
VOTE (v.): I To give v.: sammatiM dadAti (dA, c. 3.: (?).II To elect: q. v.: vfRoti (vf, c. 5.).III To provide, supply: q. v.: upakalpayati (kxp, c. 10.).
VOTE , s. sammatiH f., sammataM, sammatAsammataprakASanaM, svIkArAsvIkArapra- kASaH, sammatiKyApanaM. See SUFFRAGE.
To VOTE , v. n. sammatAsammataM prakAS (c. 10. -kASayati -yituM) or KyA in caus. (KyApayati -yituM), sammatiprakASanaM kf, sammatiM prakAS.
To VOTE , v. a. (Elect by vote) sammatipUrvvaM vf or niyuj. — (Give by vote) sammatipUrvvaM dA or pradA or pratipad.
VOTER: sammatidAyin (f. nI) and sim. comp.s.
VOTER , s. sammatiprakASakaH, sammatAsammataprakASakaH.
Votive, a. saMkalpa-saMbaMDin-datta.
VOTIVE: BaktipUrvamupAhfta (f. tA = offered) or samAhita (f. tA = put).
VOTIVE , a. vratapUrvvaM samarpitaH -tA -taM, vratAnusAreRa samarpitaH &c.
Vouch, v. t. sAkzIkf 8 U, pramARIkf, pramARaM dA 3 U. 2 dfQIkf, draQayati (D.). [Vouch]er, s. pramARapatraM-leKaH, sADanapatraM-leKaH, AgamaH.
VOUCH: I To call upon to witness: sAkzI- karoti.II To attest, confirm: q. v.: draQayati (nomi.).
To VOUCH , v. a. sAkzyeRa pramARIkf or dfQIkf, pramARaM dA.
VOUCHER: Lit. I expr. by verb.II A docu- -ment: pramARapatram.
VOUCHER , s. pramARapatraM, pramARaleKaH, sADanapatraM, sADanaleKaH, nirRayapatraM, nirRetA m. (tf), pratyayakAriRI, AgamaH.
Vouchsafe, v. t. vi-tF 1 P, kfpayA dA 3 U; (with inf.) pra-sad 1 P; See Condescend, Please; BagavAn mArIcaste darSanaM vitarati (S. 7); ‘v(ouchsafe)s thee an audience’. 2 anujYA 9 U.
VOUCHSAFE: I To permit: q. v.: anujAnAti (jYA, c. 9.).II To deign, condescend: q. v.: prasIdati (sad, c. 1.).
To VOUCHSAFE , v. a. anudA, pradA, dAtum arh (c. 1. arhati -rhituM).
To VOUCHSAFE , v. n. arh. See To DEIGN, CONDESCEND, v. n.

Vow, s. vrataM, saMkalpaH, pratijYA, SapaTaH, niyamaH; ‘under a v(ow)’ vratabadDa, Dftavrata, saMkalpa-badDa. v. pratijYA 9 A, pratijYAM kf 8 U or Aruh 1 P, saSapaTaM-sapratijYAM vad 1 P or aBi-DA 3 U, (Say, q. v.); ‘he has v(ow)ed to destroy us’ asmadvinASe kfta-saMkalposO.
VOW (subs.): (1) vrataH, -tam (= religious), breach of v.: vrataBaNgaH, K.;(2) saMkalpaH (= resolution); (3) pratijYA (= promise).
VOW (v.): pratijYAM karoti, Arjuna v. ed his death: gARqIvinA tasya vaDaH pratijYAtaH, Ve. ii.: v. To promise.

VOW , s. vrataH -taM, saNkalpaH, pratijYA, niyamaH; ‘taking a vow on one's self,’ vratasaMgrahaH; ‘faithful to one,’ saMSitavrataH -tA -taM, yatavrataH &c.; ‘violation of one,’ kzatavrataH; ‘under a vow,’ vratabadDaH -dDA -dDaM, saNkalpabadDaH &c., DftavrataH -tA -taM.
To VOW , v. a. vratapUrvvaM or saNkalpapUrvvaM pratijYA or dAtuM pratijYA or samf in caus. (-arpayati -yituM). See To PROMISE.
To VOW , v. n. (Make a vow) vrataM kf, saNkalpaM kf, pratijYAM kf, pratijYAM samAruh (c. 1. -rohati -roQuM), pratijYArohaRaM kf.
Vowel, s. svaraH, ac m., ajavarRaH.
VOWEL: (1) svaraH, short v.: hnasvasvaraH;(2) ac (t. t), ending in a v.: ajanta (f. ntA), S. k.

VOWEL , s. mAtfkA, svaraH, varRaH, acvarRaH, ajakzaraM; ‘short vowel,’ [Page833-b+ 50] hrasvasvaraH, mAtrA; ‘ending in one,’ ajantaH -ntA -ntaM; ‘long vowel,’ dIrGasvaraH, dIrGavarRaH; ‘ending in one,’ dIrGavarRAntaH &c.
Voyage, s. jalayAtrAyAnaM, samudrayAnaM, saMyAtrA. v. Ex. by kf with (s.) potena gam 1 P, jala-vartmanA gam. [Voyag]er, s. sAMyAtrikaH, jalayAtrikaH.
VOYAGE (subs.): (1) samudrayAnam (by sea);(2) jalayAtrA (by water).
VOYAGE , s. samudrayAnaM, jalayAnaM, jalayAtrA, saMyAtrA.
To VOYAGE , v. n. samudrayAnaM kf, samudreRa or jalena yA or gam.
VOYAGER , s. samudrayAyI m. (n), jalayAtrikaH, vAripaTopajIvI.

VṚIHASPATI , s. (Preceptor of the gods, and regent of the planet Jupiter. He is the son of Angiras) vfhaspatiH m., guruH m., surAcAryyaH, surapriyaH, surejyaH, gIzpatiH m., vAcaspatiH m., DizaRaH, jIvaH, ANgirasaH, citraSiKaRqijaH. His son is called BaradvAjaH.
VULCAN , s. viSvakarmmA m. (n), devaSilpI m. See VISWAKARMA.

Vulgar, a. grAmya, asaBya, aSlIla, aSizwa; prAkfta, lOkika (kI f.). [Vulgar]ism, s. grAmyA rItiH. 2 grAmyaSabdaprayogaH. [Vulgar]ity, s. asaByatA, aSlIlatA. [Vulgar]ly, adv. sADAraRataH, lOkikarItyA. 2 asaByarItyA, grAmyatayA. [Vulgar]ize, v. t. grAmyIkf.

VULGAR: (1) grAmya (f. myA = rustic), you will know that men are not v.: agrAmyatAM manuzyARAM jYAsyasi, K.; although the words......are v.: atra......SabdA grAmyA api, Kav. vii.;(2) asaBya (f. ByA = not civilized);(3) jaGanya (f. nyA = low, mean).
VULGAR , a. prAkftaH -tI -taM, asaByaH -ByA -ByaM, lOkikaH -kI -kaM, grAmyaH -myA -myaM, aSlIlaH &c., jaGanyaH &c. See COMMON, LOW.
VULGARISM: I Of manners: grAmyA rItiH, Kav. ix. 13. Of words: grAmyaH SabdaH.
VULGARISM , s. (In language) apaSabdaH, kuSabdaH.
VULGARITY: (1) grAmyatvam;(2) asaByatA;(3) jaGanyatA: v. Vulgar.
VULGARITY , s. asaByatA, aSizwatA, jaGanyatA. See LOWNESS.
VULGARIZE: (1) grAmyIkaroti.
VULGARLY: I Commonly: q. v.: sADAraRataH. II Meanly, lowly: expr. by comp.
Vulnerable, a. Bedya, Dfzya; veDya; ‘v(ulnerable) point’, raMDraM, CidraM, marman n.; AvfRodAtmano raMDraM, raMDrezu praharan ripUn (R. xviii. 61) ‘guarded against his own v(ulnerable) points’ &c.
VULNERABLE: (1) Bedya (f. dyA);(2) Dfzya (f. zyA = assailabeassailable). Ph.: v. point or part: Cidram or ranDram; well guarding all v. points: suniSCidram, Ka. xviii. 25.
VULNERABLE , a. BedyaH -dyA -dyaM, BedanIyaH &c., veDyaH &c., veDanIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘vulnerable point,’ CidraM, marmma n. (n), marmmasTAnaM.
Vulpine, a. DUrta; SfgAlavat.
VULPINE: I Lit.: by comp.: v. Fox, jackal.II Artful, crafty: DUrta (f. rtA).
Vulture, s. gfDraH, dAkzAyyaH.
VULTURE: I Lit.:(1) gfDraH;(2) SakunaH (comp., Saguna in B.).II Fig.: perh. gfDraH (from gfD: comp. eBirmantrivakEryUzmattaScOryArjitaM Danam, D. viii.
VULTURE , s. gfDraH, dAkzAyyaH, BAsaH, dUradarSI m., dIrGadarSI m.
VULTURINE: (1) comp.;(2) gADra (f. GrI: rare).

VYĀSA , s. (The arranger of the Vedas and Purānas, supposed to have lived about the 11th century after Christ. He is called ‘island-born,’ from having been born on an island in the Ganges) vyAsaH, dvEpAyanaH, kfzRadvEpAyanaH, kfzRaH.
